name: Geoplast Drainroof H6 (panel + volcanic-stone infill, installed)
epdSource: Geoplast Drainroof H6 official technical datasheet (real panel weight 3.36 kg/m2, verified 2026-07-27, corrected from an earlier ~4 kg/m2 estimate) + generic recycled-PP GWP factor (~0.58 kg CO2e/kg, Association of Plastic Recyclers) for the panel; volcanic-stone infill mass/GWP is a literature estimate (see notes) — no product-specific EPD published for either component
eolConfidenceLabel: Panel EOL scaled from a generic recycled-PP factor (not a product EPD); stone-infill EOL is an inert-waste estimate, no product-specific EPD for either
gwpConfidenceLabel: Real datasheet panel mass (3.36 kg/m2, 100% regenerated PP) + a literature estimate for the manufacturer's own specified volcanic-stone infill — not a single product EPD
notes: Real Drainroof H6 datasheet (verified 2026-07-27, PDF fetched directly): 50x50cm panels, 6cm (60mm) height, 3.36 kg/m2, 100% recycled PP — corrects this catalog's earlier ~4kg/m2, 25mm entry, which had derived thickness backward from an assumed density instead of reading the real spec. The CAD source drawing labels this layer "80mm", which matches the manufacturer's OWN typical stratigraphy (datasheet section 4): the 60mm panel is filled "over 2cm" with volcanic stone (diam. 1-12mm) above its ridges before the geotextile/substrate goes on — 60mm panel + 20mm stone fill = 80mm total installed thickness, modeled here as one combined layer rather than splitting the stone into its own series layer. Stone infill mass estimated at 1000 kg/m3 bulk density x 0.02m = 20 kg/m2 (mid-range literature value for lightweight volcanic drainage aggregate — not the geoplast-specific stone, flagged low confidence); stone GWP estimated at ~0.0075 kg CO2e/kg (literature-typical for crushed/quarried natural mineral aggregate, e.g. ICE/Ökobaudat-style gravel figures). Combined density = (3.36+20 kg/m2) / 0.08m = 292 kg/m3. Thermal conductivity kept as a nominal PP value — the layer is mostly drainage void plus loose stone, so its real R-contribution is more complex than a solid d/λ calc; included for U-value completeness anyway (see Deliverables → Assumptions), consistent with how the wall's rainscreen layers are handled.
endOfLifeScenario: Panel: reuse (durable recycled PP); stone infill: inert landfill/reuse as fill
eolAssumptionBasis: Panel EOL scaled from the original recycled-PP reuse credit by real mass (3.36/4 = 0.84x); stone infill treated as inert mineral waste — small landfill C4 figure, no recycling credit assumed (conservative, no Module D claimed for the stone portion)
